title: Tony Hangs 164.3 on Sagar, and Three Teams Share First
dek: Tony posts the week's top score and the season's biggest beatdown, Tony, Tyler and Sagar are all 6–3, and a 4–5 Clark now has 92% playoff odds.

sections.head: The lead
body: Tony scored **164.3 points** and beat Sagar by 54.1, the biggest beatdown of the season so far. The Elo ratings had Sagar 76 points higher going in, so on paper it counts as the upset of the week. In practice it was the No. 1 team in the power rankings doing what it has done lately: Tony's last three weeks average 151.5, and his all-play mark is .815, both best in the league.

The result leaves a three-way tie at the top. Tony, Tyler and Sagar are all 6–3, and Tony sits first on points with 1242.0, the most in the league. He's also, strangely, among the unlucky: he's scored like a 7.3-win team. His title odds are 35%, best in the league.

sections.head: Around the league
body: Tyler beat Kyle 134.5 to 115.4, though Kyle still leads that series 11–9. Prithvi handled Greg 131.1 to 103.1, and Clark beat Evan 146.5 to 117.5. Evan is 1–8, and his playoff odds have reached zero.
Peyton beat Stephen 128.6 to 86.6, a 42.0-point win that squares that series at 5–5. Stephen brought up the rear with 86.6 and left 27.1 points on the bench, which would not have closed the gap.

sections.head: The standings lie
body: Clark is 4–5 and has a **92% chance** of making the playoffs, up 18 points from last week. He's the league's unluckiest manager, scoring like a 5.4-win team, and he's given up more points than anyone, 1163.7. The models think the bad breaks end soon. His title odds, 23%, are nearly level with Tyler's.
Stephen is the other side of that. He's 5–4, the league's luckiest team, scoring like a 3.1-win team, and his playoff odds fell from 17% to 5%. Sagar, despite the 6–3 record, dropped from 80% to 63%.

sections.head: Power shifts
body: Tyler moved up to No. 2 and Sagar slid to No. 3. Clark jumped two spots to No. 4. Kyle fell two to No. 6, Peyton moved up one to No. 7, and Stephen dropped to No. 8.

sections.head: Game of the Week
body: Kyle vs. Sagar. Kyle is 4–5 but projected for 133.0 to Sagar's 126.4, and he's a 59% favorite. The game moves the two teams' playoff odds by a combined 46 points. Kyle needs it at 15%; Sagar needs it to stop the slide. Sagar leads the all-time series 15–6.

Clark vs. Prithvi carries 33 points of playoff odds, with Clark a 58% favorite despite trailing that series 13–8. And Peyton draws Tyler as a 6% underdog, projected 90.4 to 133.9, in a series tied 10–10.

sections.head: Award watch
body: Tyler still owns the top score of the year, 168.90 in Week 4, and the highest-scoring loss, 150.50 in Week 5. Peyton leads the waiver race thanks to Jaylen Warren's 111.8 points as a starter. Evan's Week 7, when his best lineup would have scored 151.4 instead of 90.7, is the bench blunder to beat at 60.7 points.

groupme: Week 9 is in. Tony dropped 164.3 on Sagar, the biggest beatdown of the season, and Tony, Tyler and Sagar are now all 6–3. Clark is 4–5 with 92% playoff odds. Next up: Kyle vs. Sagar, with 46 points of playoff odds on the line.
